subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should OpenClaw keep the documented first-entry default behavior and add warnings/doctor guidance, or change the default-selection contract so adding `agents.list` without `default: true` preserves implicit `main`?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but all viable fixes intentionally change documented routing semantics, warning behavior, or config-write UX, so automation should not choose the compatibility/security contract.

options.title: Warn and guide
options.body: Keep first-entry default behavior, but add config/doctor/CLI warnings and docs that make default displacement explicit before or after first `agents.list` writes.

options.title: Preserve implicit main
options.body: Change resolver or config normalization so implicit `main` stays default unless `default: true` is explicit, with migration/upgrade proof for existing configs.

options.title: Require explicit default
options.body: Reject or fail-closed on non-empty `agents.list` without a default, requiring a doctor migration and compatibility plan.

recommendation.title: Warn and guide
recommendation.body: Keep first-entry default behavior, but add config/doctor/CLI warnings and docs that make default displacement explicit before or after first `agents.list` writes.

likelyOwner.reason: The multi-agent default-routing policy introduction is the strongest available product-decision history signal.
